```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(multiScaleR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

# Choose the prediction question first

Cross-validation (CV) assesses predictions for observations excluded from model
fitting. For scale-of-effect models, the exclusion must apply to ecological
scales and learned predictor transformations as well as regression coefficients.
Fitting scales on the full data before dividing rows into folds would use
information from the assessment data.

The fold design determines the prediction question. Holding out rows at random
can assess new observations near the sampled locations. Holding out whole
animals or sites assesses transfer to excluded sampling groups. Spatial blocks
and training buffers assess predictions across a chosen geographic separation.
None of these designs automatically establishes independence or calibration.
Choose groups, block size, buffer, candidate models and scoring rules before
examining the assessment outcomes.

| Function | Use |
|:--|:--|
| `grouped_cv_folds()` | Keep whole sampling groups in one assessment fold |
| `spatial_cv_folds()` | Keep whole projected grid blocks, optionally joined by groups |
| `cross_validate()` | Refit spatial scales and GLM coefficients within each fold |
| `cross_validate_glm()` | Fit ordinary GLM reference or null models within each fold |
| `cv_tab()` | Compare pooled or per-fold held-out prediction scores |
| `select_cv()` | Evaluate model selection using training-only AIC, AICc or BIC |

# Keep dependent observations together

Use the animal, site or other sampling unit that should not occur on both sides
of a split. This small example has two observations per sampling group.

```{r grouped-folds}
ids <- paste0("record", seq_len(12))
sampling_group <- rep(letters[1:6], each = 2)
grouped <- grouped_cv_folds(sampling_group, k = 3, ids = ids)
grouped
grouped$fold1
```

Each group belongs to one assessment fold; the other groups form the analysis
set. Assignment balances row counts using whole groups, largest first. It is
deterministic and does not alter the random-number generator. If random folds
are needed, supply a predeclared explicit list of analysis/assessment IDs to the
CV functions. They also accept repeated assessment splits and training-buffer
exclusions. Both vectors must be nonempty, disjoint character IDs within a split.

Keeping a matched choice set together is necessary for step-selection designs,
but fold construction alone does not supply conditional-logistic or amt scoring.
The current scoring adapters support canonical Gaussian, Poisson and binomial
GLMs. Mixed, GAM, unmarked, Bayesian and step-selection scoring require their own
qualified predictive targets and adapters.

# Use projected spatial blocks and a training buffer

The bundled count example has 100 sampling locations. Assign stable row IDs to
both the response data and the point object. The bundled locations are an
unreferenced simulated grid. For this example, define its Cartesian distances
in meters with an explicit local CRS. This is not a claim about real geographic
locations. Real data need their actual projected CRS, with an explicit transform
when necessary; never relabel longitude/latitude as linear coordinates. No
full-data centering or scaling is performed below.

```{r spatial-folds}
data("landscape_counts")
data("surv_pts")
dat <- landscape_counts
locations <- surv_pts
stopifnot(is.na(sf::st_crs(locations)))
local_crs <- paste0('LOCAL_CS["Simulated metre grid",LOCAL_DATUM["Local",0],',
                    'UNIT["metre",1],AXIS["X",EAST],AXIS["Y",NORTH]]')
sf::st_crs(locations) <- local_crs
ids <- paste0("site", seq_len(nrow(dat)))
rownames(dat) <- rownames(locations) <- ids
xy <- sf::st_coordinates(locations)
dat$east <- xy[, 1]

# Distances use the projected CRS units. Inspect them before choosing distances.
sf::st_crs(locations)$units_gdal
folds <- spatial_cv_folds(locations, block_size = 1000, k = 3, buffer = 100)
folds
```

An assessment fold can contain several disjoint blocks. The generator balances
counts; it does not create contiguous regions. With a positive buffer, the
training set excludes an entire spatial unit if any point in that unit lies
within the requested distance of an assessment point. The buffer measures
point-to-point separation, not distance to whole block boundaries.

Inspect `attr(folds, "fold_info")$assignment` for row, block, unit and fold
assignments and `$excluded` for training IDs removed per fold. For repeated
sampling, pass `group = dat$animal` or another aligned group vector. Blocks
connected by a shared group are joined, including transitive connections. If
too few units remain for `k` folds, or buffering removes every training unit,
the generator stops before model fitting. Coordinate tables require an explicit
projected `crs`; geographic coordinates are rejected rather than interpreted as
linear distances.

# Compare predictions from the same assessment targets

Start with inexpensive reference models. The trend below uses native `poly()`
metadata learned from each training set. The null model uses the same rows,
folds and Poisson observation definition.

```{r reference-models}
candidates <- list(
  null = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ 1, dat, folds, family = "poisson",
                            keep_fits = TRUE),
  trend = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ poly(east, 2), dat, folds, family = "poisson",
                             keep_fits = TRUE)
)
vapply(candidates, function(x) x$complete, logical(1))
cv_tab(candidates, metric = "neg_log_score")
cv_tab(candidates, metric = "rmse", by_fold = TRUE)
```

Lower scores are better. Negative log scores retain the Poisson count
probability, including its constants. RMSE is the square root of pooled squared
errors across assessment occurrences, not the average of fold RMSEs. If an
observation is assessed repeatedly, every occurrence contributes to the pooled
score. Frequency weights retain their replication meaning.

Binomial input can be numeric/logical 0/1, a two-level factor, or
`cbind(successes, failures)`. Binomial negative log scores compare count
probabilities; Brier scores average squared error over individual trials and
weight observations by frequency times trial count. A zero-trial row contributes
no score. An observed event assigned zero probability produces an infinite log
loss, which is retained without clipping.

`cv_tab()` requires matching analysis and assessment IDs, observed responses,
trials and frequency weights. It rejects incomplete candidates rather than
dropping failed folds. Inspect `$errors`, `$warnings` and `$diagnostics` before
interpreting scores. Completion means the requested calculations finished, not
that numerical diagnostics or calibration passed. Scores add no complexity
penalty and are not AIC values, Akaike weights or model probabilities. Variation
across dependent folds is not an independent-observation standard error.

# Evaluate a model-selection procedure within the folds

Per-fold assessment ranks describe prediction performance. They must not choose
the model whose predictions are then scored on those same observations.
`select_cv()` instead uses the retained **training fits**, selecting by a
predeclared AIC, AICc or BIC rule and then retrieving the chosen model's held-out
predictions. No extra fitting is needed.

```{r training-selection}
selected <- select_cv(candidates, criterion = "AICc", ties = "first")
selected$selection$chosen
selected$selection$tables$fold1
cv_tab(c(candidates, list(training_selected = selected)), metric = "neg_log_score")
```

The native training tables retain their original parameter counts. Estimated
scales and shapes enter the existing multiScaleR penalty; fixed radii remain
fixed. Native nuisance parameters and likelihood-comparability guards are
unchanged. This example predeclares that exact criterion ties use the first
listed model. The default `ties = "error"` retains an unresolved tie as a failed
selection fold. Invalid or nonfinite training criteria are also retained as
failures, leaving the procedure's pooled scores incomplete.

The resulting score assesses this candidate set and selection rule. If pooled
CV results are used to choose the candidate set, kernel, block size or selection
rule itself, assess that final choice with an independent test set or a further
outer validation layer. Neither `cv_tab()` nor `select_cv()` integrates parameter
or selection uncertainty, supplies observation intervals or establishes
calibration.

# Add a model that estimates ecological scales

Reuse the same explicit folds with raw-cell preparation. This workflow is not
run during vignette builds because it adds a scale optimization for every fold.
The test suite checks training-only scale refitting and score agreement with
native GLMs. Choose the extraction domain and initial scales independently of
assessment outcomes.

```{r estimated-scales, eval=FALSE}
land <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif", package = "multiScaleR"))
# The example raster uses the same simulated grid and local distance declaration.
terra::crs(land) <- sf::st_crs(locations)$wkt
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = locations, raster_stack = land,
                      max_D = 1500, sigma = c(250, 500, 250),
                      store_cell_data = TRUE)
# Prepared and response rows must have exactly the same IDs and order.
stopifnot(identical(rownames(inputs$kernel_dat), rownames(dat)))
spatial <- cross_validate(counts ~ land1 + land2, dat, inputs, folds,
                          family = "poisson", keep_fits = TRUE)
models <- c(candidates, list(spatial = spatial))
cv_tab(models, metric = "neg_log_score")
selection <- select_cv(models, criterion = "AICc", ties = "first")
```

`cross_validate()` rebuilds spatial predictors inside every training set,
estimates scales and coefficients there, and freezes its learned normalization
and bin references for assessment prediction. It preserves existing starts,
cold/limiting/curvature checks and metric/kernel guards. Do not supply full-data
scale fits as substitutes for fold fits. Ordinary reference models use
`cross_validate_glm()`; the spatial entry point still requires an optimized
spatial predictor. Grouped fold generation is distinct from grouped raster
preparation. The former defines sampling units for validation; the latter
chooses a fixed covariate map for each row.

## Use fixed maps for different raster groups

Modern `kernel_prep_by_group()` inputs retain raw buffers and a named
`raster_group` mapping. CV validates this mapping before fitting, subsets it
with the buffers and records analysis/assessment assignments in `$raster_groups`.
Training normalization and bin references still use training rows only.

```{r grouped-raster-cv, eval=FALSE}
# Both labels use the same simulated map here solely to illustrate alignment.
# For real data, supply the appropriate maps with identical grids and layer names.
maps <- list(map1 = land, map2 = land)
map_id <- rep(c("map1", "map2"), length.out = nrow(locations))
group_inputs <- kernel_prep_by_group(locations, maps, group = map_id,
                                    max_D = 1500, store_cell_data = TRUE)
grouped_cv <- cross_validate(counts ~ land1 + land2, dat, group_inputs, folds,
                             family = "poisson")
grouped_cv$raster_groups$fold1
```

Raster-map labels do not themselves introduce annual random effects, varying
scales or extra fitted parameters. Explicit formula factors/interactions and
estimated scales/shapes keep their native parameter penalties. A held-out factor
level absent from training still produces the native prediction failure; CV does
not replace it with a zero effect. Inspect the selected row/map records and
`$selection$candidate_settings` when evaluating a training-selection procedure.
`$settings$controls_from` identifies the first candidate whose control fields
are inherited; candidate-specific controls remain in the selection record.

## Retain cells intersecting the extraction buffer

Native raster preparation records both cell dimensions. A cell can intersect
the extraction buffer even when its center lies beyond the nominal radius.
CV retains those values and fixes the bin domain using the requested radius
plus half the pixel diagonal, rather than a maximum learned from held-out rows.
Representative distances and normalization are still learned only from training
rows. Geometry is frozen with the bin reference. Legacy saved inputs without
cell geometry keep the original strict gate; prepare them again with the current
constructor if that gate rejects their cell-center distances. Extraction,
kernel/metric definitions and fitted parameter bounds are unchanged.

# Keep outputs proportionate to the task

Both CV functions default to `keep_fits = FALSE`, retaining compact scores,
training summaries and diagnostics. Full fold fits are needed by `select_cv()`;
request them only when evaluating a training-based selection procedure or
inspecting fits. `select_cv()` returns compact output by default. Reuse the
same prepared inputs and fold list across candidates, and avoid saving duplicate
rasters or arrays of fit objects as intermediate checkpoints.

For inference-target and interval distinctions, see
`vignette("inference-contracts", package = "multiScaleR")`. For likelihood-based
model comparison, see `?aic_tab` and `?bic_tab`. Function help for `?cross_validate`,
`?spatial_cv_folds`, `?cv_tab` and `?select_cv` gives the complete input and
result contracts.
